public_rationale: The evidence supports a substantial threat to agreement on 10 November. IAPP reports that opposition to foundation-model rules caused Parliament representatives to end a meeting early, and records a parliamentary adviser's very pessimistic assessment of that moment. Hogan Lovells independently dates the impasse and uncertainty to the same day. This supports serious jeopardy in its ordinary sense. It does not establish the separate suggestion of regulatory capture or predict that negotiations must ultimately fail.
limitations: The assessment relies on reporting and legal analysis because official meeting records were not obtained.
The adviser's probability estimate was a participant's judgment, not an independently measured likelihood.
Later improvements in the negotiations do not establish their condition at the time of the post.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The draft EU AI Act is in serious jeopardy as of November 2023.

statement.excerpt: Breaking news: the draft EU AI Act—the closest thing we have to AI regulation with real teeth—is in serious jeopardy, potentially a direct victim of regulatory capture, governments doing the bidding of those they are supposed govern.

our_interpretation: Assess the negotiating situation on 10 November 2023, the post date. This is an immediate observation, not a prediction that the Act would ultimately fail.
The ordinary reading of serious jeopardy is a substantial threat to securing agreement, evidenced by a breakdown in negotiations or unresolved opposition over essential provisions.
The separate, qualified suggestion of regulatory capture is outside this claim's normalized proposition.
criteria.support_condition: Negotiating records or credible reporting establish that substantive opposition had disrupted negotiations and materially threatened agreement as of 10 November 2023.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Records establish that the alleged breakdown or substantive opposition did not occur, or that agreement was secure and the remaining disagreements were routine.

His improved assessment and the rapporteur's optimism on 15 November concern subsequent developments.
